lessons.title: Lending to the government
lessons.summary: Who issues T-bills and T-bonds, and why they're considered low-risk.

cards.title: Who issues them
cards.body: The Government of Sri Lanka borrows by selling Treasury bills and bonds, managed by the Central Bank's Public Debt Department. Buying one means lending to the government.

cards.title: Why low-risk
cards.body: They're seen as the lowest-risk rupee investment, because the government can raise taxes or borrow to repay in rupees. Low-risk isn't no-risk, but it's lower than a company or a bank.

cards.title: How to buy
cards.body: Individuals usually buy through a primary dealer or a bank's treasury desk. The government sells new ones at regular auctions.

quiz.question: Buying a T-bill means you are…
options: Buying a share of the government
quiz.explanation: You're a lender; the government repays you.

quiz.question: Why are government securities considered low-risk?
options: The government can repay in its own currency

quiz.question: Who manages the issuing of T-bills and T-bonds?
options: The Central Bank's Public Debt Department
quiz.explanation: The Central Bank runs the auctions.

cards.title: 91, 182 or 364 days
cards.body: T-bills are short-term: about 3, 6 or 12 months.

cards.title: Sold at a discount
cards.body: There's no interest payment. You pay less than the face value now, and get the full face value at maturity. The gap is your return.

cards.title: Example
cards.body: A Rs 100,000 364-day bill at an 8.65% yield costs about Rs 92,060 today. At maturity you get Rs 100,000 (less 10% tax on the Rs 7,940 gain in the trainer).

quiz.question: How does a T-bill pay you?
options: You buy below face value and receive face value at maturity
quiz.explanation: That's what 'sold at a discount' means.

quiz.question: Which is NOT a standard T-bill tenure?
A higher yield on a new T-bill means you pay…
options: Less today for the same face value

cards.title: 2 to 20 years
cards.body: T-bonds last much longer than bills. In the trainer you can choose 2, 5 or 10 years.

cards.title: Coupons
cards.body: A bond pays a fixed coupon every 6 months. A Rs 100,000 bond with a 10% coupon pays Rs 5,000 twice a year, and your Rs 100,000 back at maturity.

cards.title: Auctions
cards.body: Investors bid the yields they want; the government accepts the lowest-cost bids it needs. The results set the going rate for that tenure.

quiz.question: A Rs 200,000 bond has a 9% coupon. Each 6-monthly coupon (before tax) is…
How often do T-bonds pay coupons?
At a bond auction, investors bid…

lessons.title: Yields, prices and selling early
lessons.summary: When rates rise, existing bond prices fall.

cards.title: The seesaw
cards.body: Your bond pays a fixed coupon. If new bonds start paying more, nobody will pay full price for yours — its price drops. If rates fall, your bond is worth more.

cards.title: Hold to maturity
cards.body: If you hold until maturity, price changes along the way don't matter: you get every coupon and your face value back.

cards.title: Selling early
cards.body: Sell before maturity and you get today's market price — a loss if rates have risen since you bought. This is interest-rate risk. Longer bonds feel it more.

quiz.question: Market yields rise after you buy a bond. Its price…
quiz.explanation: Its fixed coupon looks worse than new bonds.

quiz.question: You hold a bond to maturity. What do you get?
options: All coupons and the face value
quiz.explanation: Price swings only matter if you sell early.

quiz.question: Which bond is hit harder by a rate rise?
quiz.explanation: Longer bonds have more coupons at the old rate.

cards.title: Who you lend to
cards.body: An FD is a loan to a bank or finance company; a T-bill is a loan to the government. The government is generally seen as the safer borrower.

cards.title: Rates
cards.body: Some finance companies pay more than T-bills, while big banks often pay less. Compare after-tax rates for the same period.

cards.title: Flexibility
cards.body: T-bills and bonds can be sold before maturity at the market price. FDs can be broken early, usually with an interest penalty.

quiz.question: A T-bill is a loan to…
quiz.explanation: FDs are loans to banks or finance companies.

quiz.question: To compare a 1-year T-bill and a 12-month FD fairly, compare…
options: Their after-tax returns for the same period

quiz.question: What usually happens if you need your FD money early?
options: You can't get it at all
